harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a DHCP relay chain so node3 obtains its address from the DHCP service on node2, despite node2 and node3 sitting on different L2 segments off node1. Assigned node1's eth1 (192.168.21.1/24, facing node2) and eth2 (192.168.22.1/24, facing node3) as gateways with IP forwarding enabled; gave node2 a static address (192.168.21.10/24) on its segment-facing NIC; installed and configured Kea DHCP4 on node2 with a relayed subnet declaration for 192.168.22.0/24 (giaddr 192.168.22.1, pool .100-.200, routers 192.168.22.1); installed and configured isc-dhcp-relay (dhcrelay) on node1 listening on eth1+eth2 and forwarding to node2's 192.168.21.10. Verified node3 obtained 192.168.22.100 via the relay and confirmed the lease recorded on node2. All configuration was made persistent (interfaces.d static stanzas, sysctl.d forwarding, systemd-enabled kea-dhcp4 and isc-dhcp-relay services). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and health baselines on all three nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via native reboot commands, polled each until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified post-restart recovery — node1's static addressing/forwarding/dhcrelay all came back automatically, node2's kea-dhcp4 service and prior lease data survived, and node3 automatically re-acquired its DHCP-relayed address (192.168.22.100) from node2 with no manual intervention after its reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1 (SONiC/Debian) has eth1 facing node2's enp8s0 and eth2 facing node3's enp8s0, previously unaddressed/unbridged segments
Assigned node1 eth1=192.168.21.1/24, eth2=192.168.22.1/24 and enabled ip_forward + per-interface forwarding
Set node2 enp8s0 static to 192.168.21.10/24 via nmcli

Installed Kea DHCP4 (kea package) on node2, configured /etc/kea/kea-dhcp4.conf with a relayed subnet4 declaration for 192.168.22.0/24 (relay ip-addresses 192.168.22.1, pool .100-.200, routers 192.168.22.1), enabled+started kea-dhcp4.service, opened firewalld dhcp service

Installed isc-dhcp-relay on node1, configured /etc/default/isc-dhcp-relay (SERVERS=192.168.21.10, INTERFACES='eth1 eth2'), enabled+started isc-dhcp-relay.service, verified dhcrelay bound to UDP 67 on both interfaces
Triggered DHCP renewal on node3's enp8s0 and confirmed it obtained 192.168.22.100 via the relay; confirmed lease recorded in node2's kea-leases4.csv
Persisted node1 addressing via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1-eth2-static and /etc/sysctl.d/99-relay-forwarding.conf so config survives reboot
Captured pre-restart boot_id/health baseline on node1, node2, node3
Restarted node1 (reboot), polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified static IPs/forwarding/dhcrelay auto-recovered
Restarted node2 (systemctl reboot), polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified static IP and kea-dhcp4 service + lease data recovered
Restarted node3 (systemctl reboot), polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified it automatically re-obtained 192.168.22.100 via the relay chain with no manual steps

evidence.requirement: node3 obtains its address from node2's DHCP service despite segment separation via node1
evidence.summary: Kea DHCP4 installed/configured on node2 for relayed subnet 192.168.22.0/24; isc-dhcp-relay installed/configured/running on node1 relaying eth1<->eth2 to 192.168.21.10; node3 renewed and obtained 192.168.22.100/24 with the lease recorded on node2 keyed to node3's MAC/hostname

Backgrounded reboot command returned ack before disconnection

eth1/eth2 static IPs, forwarding sysctls, and isc-dhcp-relay/dhcrelay process all auto-recovered without manual intervention

Backgrounded systemctl reboot returned ack before disconnection

evidence.requirement: node2 changed boot identity and recovered state post-restart
evidence.summary: New boot_id 43f08855-...; static IP, kea-dhcp4.service active, and prior lease data (192.168.22.100 for node3) all recovered
Captured boot_id cce73776-... with its DHCP-obtained address 192.168.22.100/24 in place
Backgrounded systemctl reboot returned ack before disconnection

evidence.summary: New boot_id 7a01f4ff-...; enp8s0 automatically re-acquired 192.168.22.100/24 via DHCP through the relay chain on fresh boot, with no manual steps
